column1: # Every row is a case where this library and ICU disagree and the
# disagreement is expected. A new one fails the build; a row that stops
# reproducing fails too. An ICU version bump regenerates this file, and
# the diff is the point rather than a nuisance.

column7: note

ICU_REDERIVES_FROM_AVAILABLE_FORMATS. ICU does not render the locale's standard time pattern when an hc keyword is present. It reads the skeleton off that pattern and asks DateTimePatternGenerator for a pattern again, so the answer comes from availableFormats and carries that table's widths, literals and day period field rather than the standard pattern's. This library renders the locale's own standard pattern with the hour written in the cycle named and nothing else touched, so the two differ wherever the two tables differ in anything but the hour. This locale has no time row in datetime-patterns, so naming a cycle is what created this one. See docs/boundaries.md, what an explicit hour cycle changes.

ICU_SUBSTITUTES_THE_DAY_PERIOD. zh-Hant states Bh:mm as both its standard short time and its hm item, so this library renders the flexible day period the locale asks for and reads 凌晨 at half past midnight. ICU re-derives from availableFormats once hc is present, asks for a skeleton that does not name B, and a request without B is answered with a even where the matching entry states B, so it reads 上午. Its own getBestPattern shows it with no cycle named at all: Bhm gives Bh:mm and hm gives ah:mm, from the same data. This is not a parent chain difference: release-78.3 states %%Parent{root} in zh_Hant.txt, the same parent CLDR's parentLocales gives, and that file's gregorian hm is Bh:mm. The hour itself agrees under every cycle, and at 15:30 both day periods read 下午 so the difference does not show. See docs/boundaries.md, what an explicit hour cycle changes.
